newsitem.title: UK: Granada in agreed bid for Yorkshire-Tyne.
newsitem.headline: Granada in agreed bid for Yorkshire-Tyne.

text.p: Britain's Granada Group Plc said on Wednesday it was making an agreed bid to fully take over Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc in a move valuing Yorkshire at 711 million pounds ($1.2 billion).

Media to leisure group Granada, which already owns 27 percent of Yorkshire-Tyne Tees, said the offer of two new Granada shares and 1,825.32 pence in cash for every three Yorkshire shares valued Yorkshire ordinary shares at 1,175 pence each. They closed at 1,155 pence on Tuesday.
The offer had been widely flagged and Granada chairman Gerry Robinson said earlier this month that the two companies had agreed on 11.75 pounds ($19.59) per share as an outline price.
The companies said that Yorkshire will pay an interim dividend of 7.5 pence.

Robinson said in Wednesday's statement on the takeover, "Granada and Yorkshire's existing airtime and international programme sales arrangements, underpinned by our 27 per cent shareholding, provide a solid foundation for a merger between the two companies. We believe that the strategic arguments in favour of the combination are both powerful and widely accepted."
Granada, whose interests span broadcasting, leisure, hotels and catering, owns the independent television (ITV) franchise for north-west England, which is adjacent to Yorkshire's area.

Ward Thomas, chairman of Yorkshire, said, "By the beginning of this year Yorkshire-Tyne Tees had fully recovered from the problems that beset the company in 1993. However, Yorkshire is operating in an increasingly competitive world."

Ward said ITV had seen a significant decrease in its share of television revenue and said that the company now believed a combination with Granada's broadcasting business was in the best interests of shareholders and would safeguard Yorkshire's future.
The deal will need regulatory approval, and Robinson said earlier this month he believed it would take some two months to complete even if everything went smoothly. ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
